events.text: An imagined copper astrolabe on indigo cloth, sparked by the Met astrolabe record. Goal: reserve blue openings between warm arcs and keep the brightest light compact at one pivot. I will develop this in small animated batches, looking whole and close.
The first washes leave three pale horizontal seams. I will overlap those and give the bottom cloth a continuous blue-violet field before drawing metal.
The overlaps close the bright seams; gentle wash bands remain. A broad soft cast shadow and four joined dark arcs will place the tilted instrument without filling its blue center.
The dark ring is joined and the blue center stays open. Its lower edge is heavy; four narrower warm faces can turn the band into metal while leaving the lower shadow quiet.
The narrower warm faces sit inside the shadow rim and leave an uneven useful edge. I will add a small open suspension loop and its short copper bridge above the ring.
The top loop is small and clear at whole view; the default close crop misses it. Inside, a diagonal rule and two bowed rails will establish the instrument while reserving broad blue windows.

The inner arc has a deliberate left gap, but its ends look detached. I will tie them to the outer ring with two short supports and add one off-axis curved rail; the large openings should remain legible.
The supports now meet the ring. The diagonal crossings are readable but flat; a smaller offset ellipse, lower bow and dark pivot can give the openwork depth without filling every space.
The offset ellipse is visible and the pivot has a small warm face. The lowest bow ends freely on the left; I will connect that end, then add three tapered star pointers with unequal reach.

The pointers read as small tapered tabs at whole view, though their roots remain blunt close up. Four cool, subdued turns will separate metal planes; I will keep these shorter than the warm structural gestures.
The cool turns read as patina rather than broad reflections. The rim is still bare; a sparse scale can suggest measurement while leaving the upper warm arc quieter than a fully engraved border.
The first scale marks survive whole view and do not merge into the rails. I will leave a breathing gap over the suspension bridge and carry four marks across the right shoulder.
The upper scale stays readable around the openwork. Four quieter marks down the right rim will turn into shadow instead of keeping equal contrast all around.
The right scale loses contrast into patina as intended. Four bottom divisions will remain subdued; then the engraving can stop before it competes with the pivot.

The lower divisions are appropriately quiet. I will test one short 8px loaded ivory stroke on the pivot before changing its width; the light needs to survive whole view without spreading across the rule.
The 8px pivot light is already visible at whole view and stays compact; I will keep it. Broader warm shoulder planes can give the ring body without extending that brightest value.
The pivot remains the smallest bright accent. The cloth still reads as horizontal wash bands; four long, low-contrast folds will give the instrument a place to rest without enclosing it.

The watery folds barely change the dry bands at whole view. I will try two thin-oil folds in related violets, plus a soft contact band below the rim; the comparison changes medium and is not controlled.
The oil folds show, but the contact band floats below the instrument. A wider low-load bridge should join shadow to rim; I will inspect that single repair before more details.

The broader shadow bridge now meets the rim at whole view, though it retains regular ridges. The diagonal rule needs its own scale; four short divisions on the upper half should help distinguish it from the curved openwork.
The rule divisions read as dark notches close up. Two more toward its lower end, plus a pair of small dark fittings at the endpoints, can finish that structure without adding a second bright focus.

The endpoint fittings stay small. Beginning refinement: I will give each fitting a muted warm face, lighten one side of the suspension bridge, and soften the blunt lower star-pointer root with a short curve.
The fittings remain quieter than the pivot; the lower pointer root is rounder but still thick. This upper review checks the suspension loop and bridge outside the default middle crop.

The upper crop shows a small angular loop and a filled bridge with regular ridges. I will soften one loop shoulder with a sampled warm arc, keep its blue hole, and reduce the heaviest pointer root with a related warm face.

The loop shoulder is warmer and remains open; the pointer root is still a broad tab, so more tracing would mainly thicken it. This lower pan checks the rim contact and fold ends before deciding the final two adjustments.

The lower pan confirms contact, but the shadow repair has parallel ridges and the lower-left green turn is stripe-like. Two restrained warm/cool faces will reduce those color contrasts; they will not erase relief.

Finished at88 completed marks after refinement79–88. The blue openings remain open, warm shoulder faces turn the ring, and the single8px loaded pivot light survives whole view. The shadow bridge70 restores contact. Covers87–88 reduce color contrast but retain relief; angular joins, blunt pointer roots, regular bristles and wash bands remain. Further engraving would crowd the openings and tracing would thicken edges, so I am stopping without padding.

creation.method: Original browser-painted study in animated 1–4-stroke adaptive batches using visible score controls, settled whole/close screenshots and live-written easel notes. No full score prepared ahead.
creation.finalReview: Deliberate refinement79–88; paired whole/close88, actual900x620PNG, upper82 and lower86 pans.
creation.notes: All easel thoughts written live during painting; title assigned through an empty score before final JSON export and broadcast end.
limitations: Initial camera/selector timeouts at4 and8 were recovered without repeating paint. Eight-mark review was recaptured before9. At12 a camera transition was caught at1.6×; paired review was repeated after settling before13. Subsequent camera helper polls the displayed target before capture.
Initial inspection automation used a stale mark-counter value; actual DOM mark count and playback-at-rest were checked, helper corrected to explicit counts. No painting was duplicated.
Unsupported note kind look at82 failed before sharing; corrected to notice. Default middle close crop clips suspension and contact; upper82 and lower86 pans inspect those areas.
PNG exported before naming/end; final titledJSON after end exactly matches ended public document. ActualPNG unchanged by naming.
Angular joins, blunt pointer roots, regular bristle ridges, wash bands and ridged contact repair remain. Stopped88 because more engraving crowds openings and tracing thickens edges; count not padded.
